newsitem.title: USA: Indiana corn, soy stage rapid growth last week.
newsitem.headline: Indiana corn, soy stage rapid growth last week.

text.p: Corn and soybean plants grew rapidly during the week ended Sunday under hot and sunny conditions, according to the Indiana Agricultural Statistics Service.

As of Sunday, the corn crop improved to a rating of 70 percent good to excellent, above the 62 percent in that category the previous week. Twenty-three percent of the crop was fair and seven percent was poor to very poor.
Soybean planting was 99 percent complete and 65 percent of the crop was good to excellent, 27 percent fair and eight percent poor to very poor.

Wheat harvest was moving into full swing in southern Indiana, where much of the wheat acreage is located for that state. Wheat was 15 percent harvested, above four percent a week ago but behind 37 percent a year ago and also behind 33 percent average.
Topsoil moisture was rated 13 percent surplus, 78 percent adequate and nine percent short. Subsoil moisture was 14 percent surplus, 80 percent adequate and six percent short.
Pasture conditions were 10 percent excellent, 62 percent good, 21 percent fair, six percent poor and one percent very poor.
